title: Demo FAQ (Internal) — Redwood Inference
content:
Purpose
- This is the internal FAQ used by AEs/SEs during live demos and follow-ups. It’s designed to keep answers consistent, reduce "let me check" moments, and make escalation paths obvious.
- Audience: AEs, SEs, CSMs supporting demo → POC handoff.
- Scope: Hosted API + Dedicated controls + Private/VPC talking points.

House rules for live answers
1) Be specific about what’s true today vs roadmap. If unsure, use the safe fallback phrasing: “We support that in certain tiers/deployments—let’s confirm what applies to your environment.”
2) Don’t quote hard benchmark numbers unless they’re on the approved slide/deck. When asked, pivot to how we measure + what levers we expose.
3) No customer data. Demo tenant is synthetic. Don’t imply the graphs are from real customers.
4) If the question is procurement/security, offer the security FAQ link + suggest a follow-up security call.

Escalation contacts (who to ping)
- Demo environment broken / reset failing / dashboards empty: Markus Klein (Demo technical owner) + #eng-platform (also check the reset runbook)
- Latency / reliability / SLO / incident history: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead)
- Routing/fallback behavior details: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- SDK snippets / examples / version pins: Alex Martinez / Monica Patel
- Security/compliance (SOC2, audit logs, retention, residency, DPA): Naomi Feldman (security/compliance advisor) + Marcus Lin (security engineering reviewer)
- Messaging/competitive framing: Soojin Lee (PMM) + Camila Reyes (Marketing sponsor)
- Pricing/credits approvals (POC, Dedicated commits): follow pricing guidance doc; escalate to Stephanie Nguyen (NA) / Lukas Meyer (EMEA) if discounting/credits exception is requested


SECTION A — "What is Redwood?" (positioning / why us)

Q: “Are you a model provider?”
A (recommended): “We’re an inference platform. We help teams run and optimize LLM inference reliably—hosted, dedicated capacity, or private deployments—so you can meet latency/cost/reliability targets without rebuilding the serving stack.”
Follow-up prompt: “Are you optimizing for latency, cost, or deployment constraints (VPC/on-prem)?”

Q: “So why not just use [cloud managed endpoints]?”
A (recommended): “Many teams start there. Where Redwood shows up is production economics and operational control: predictable latency under load, cost levers like batching/caching/quantization profiles, observability down to tokens, and controlled rollouts/fallback policies across regions and model variants.”
Safe proof phrasing: “We’ll show the knobs and the measurement, not just a single point benchmark.”

Q: “How do you compare to an LLM API provider?”
A: “If you need a simple API with minimal controls, those can be great. Redwood is for teams that need more control over throughput/latency, need stable model pinning and rollouts, or need dedicated/private deployment options. Same API surface, but you can evolve deployment mode as requirements tighten.”


SECTION B — Demo tenant realities (set expectations without undermining)

Q: “Is this production?”
A: “It’s a production-like demo tenant with synthetic data. We pin model versions and seed realistic traffic so you can see dashboards, rollouts, and failure modes. In a POC, we’ll use your prompts and success criteria.”

Q: “Are the dashboards showing real customers?”
A: “No—synthetic usage generated for demo reliability. The point is to show what you’d get in your own org and what metrics we expose.”

Q: “Can we share demo keys with our team?”
A: “We keep demo keys least-privilege and time-bounded. For a customer team, we’ll create a separate POC tenant or scoped access. If you need temporary access for evaluation, we can set it up with controls and rotation.”
Escalate: Markus Klein + Ethan Park for access/RBAC questions.


SECTION C — Latency / throughput / performance

Q: “What latency should we expect?”
A: “It depends on the model, context length, output length, and concurrency. What we can commit to is a process: we baseline your workload, then tune batching/caching/routing to hit your SLOs. We also expose percentiles and token-level breakdowns so you can see where time and cost go.”
Avoid: quoting one p50 number unless it’s on approved deck.

Q: “How do you handle load spikes?”
A: “Three layers: (1) continuous batching and cache management in the runtime, (2) autoscaling / capacity policies (hosted + dedicated options), and (3) routing/fallback policies to keep the app online when a region or variant is constrained.”

Q: “Do you support streaming? Does it drop?”
A: “Yes—streaming is supported. If a stream disconnect happens, clients can resume by retrying with idempotency/replay patterns depending on your integration. In the demo we also show retries and graceful handling.”
If prospect flags EU streaming instability: “We’ve seen region-specific edge cases and have mitigations; we can share current status and recommended client settings.”
Escalate: Sean Gallagher + Alex Martinez.

Q: “How do you prevent noisy-neighbor issues?”
A: “Dedicated capacity is the cleanest story: isolated GPU pools and predictable throughput. In hosted, we use admission control, rate limits, and routing policies to protect the fleet.”


SECTION D — Reliability / routing / fallback

Q: “What happens if the model is unavailable?”
A: “You can define fallback policies: compatible model variants within a family, alternate regions, or a smaller/cheaper variant to maintain uptime. The goal is graceful degradation with observability so you know it happened.”
Demo-friendly phrasing: “We prefer ‘stay online with known behavior’ over ‘hard fail’.”

Q: “Can we pin to a specific model version?”
A: “Yes. You can pin versions for stability and do controlled rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback if error/latency thresholds are exceeded.”

Q: “Will you swap models under us?”
A: “Not without your policy. Hosted has a catalog that evolves, but you control route pins and rollouts. In dedicated/private, you typically have even stronger control.”


SECTION E — Observability / Console questions

Q: “What do you measure?”
A: “Latency percentiles, throughput, error rates, token usage and cost breakdowns, and route/model-level analytics. We also support tracing hooks and rollout views so you can correlate changes to outcomes.”

Q: “Can we export logs/metrics to our stack?”
A: “Yes in supported tiers—common patterns include SIEM export for audit events and metrics integrations for operational telemetry. We’ll confirm which integrations you need (Datadog, Splunk, etc.) and what’s in-scope for your deployment.”
Escalate: Allison Grant + Logan Wright.

Q: “Why do I sometimes see empty graphs in demos?”
A: “The demo dashboards depend on the synthetic traffic generator and correct project selection/time range. If it’s empty, we can kick the generator and re-run the healthcheck.”
SE quick fix: run demo healthcheck + synthetic traffic job; then refresh Console.
Escalate: Markus Klein.


SECTION F — Pricing / packaging / POC credits (high-risk section)

Q: “How do you charge?”
A: “Hosted API is usage-based (tokens/embedding units). Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits) for predictable throughput and isolation. Private deployments are a platform fee + support tier.”

Q: “What’s the ROI lever?”
A: “Two main levers: reduce per-token cost (batching/caching/quantization and model selection) and reduce operational overhead (reliability tooling, rollouts, observability). We focus on unit economics you can measure.”

Q: “Can you match [competitor] pricing?”
A: “We can review total cost for your workload—token price alone is rarely apples-to-apples due to batching, cache hit rates, and output quality. If you have a target, we’ll validate it with a short benchmark on your prompts.”
Escalation: Do not negotiate live. Offer to set up a pricing follow-up. Use pricing guidance doc; for exceptions, escalate to Stephanie Nguyen / Lukas Meyer.

Q: “Do you offer POC credits?”
A: “Often, yes—within guardrails and tied to a success plan (prompts/evals, throughput target, timeline). We’ll align on success criteria and then confirm the credit package.”

Q: “What’s the difference between ‘Dedicated’ and ‘Private’?”
A: “Dedicated is reserved capacity managed by us, typically in our cloud environment, with isolation and predictable throughput. Private is deployment in your network boundary (VPC/on-prem options) with tighter control over networking and compliance requirements.”


SECTION G — Security / compliance (answer confidently, then offer artifacts)

Q: “Do you train on our data?”
A: “No. We don’t use customer prompts or outputs to train foundation models. Data is processed to provide the service and may be retained based on your configured retention settings and support needs.”
Offer: “We can walk through retention controls and what gets logged.”

Q: “Is data encrypted?”
A: “Yes—encryption in transit and at rest. For Private/VPC and certain tiers, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations.”
Escalate for exact details: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin.

Q: “Do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC?”
A: “Yes—SSO/SAML for enterprise access control and RBAC for least-privilege. We can show the Console flows (or screenshots) and explain role mappings.”

Q: “Do you have audit logs?”
A: “Yes—admin and access-relevant events are captured in audit logs. For demos, we can show a sanitized example and explain how it exports to your compliance workflow.”
Safety: In demos, avoid showing any internal employee emails/user IDs beyond what’s needed.

Q: “What about data residency?”
A: “We can support region selection for where workloads run. For strict residency or regulated workloads, Private/VPC options are usually the right fit. We’ll confirm your required regions and constraints.”
EMEA note: If they ask for specific countries, don’t improvise. Offer a follow-up with the current region list and roadmap.

Q: “Can you sign a DPA?”
A: “Yes—standard enterprise process. We’ll loop in our legal/security team as part of procurement.”


SECTION H — Private deployment / VPC / on-prem questions

Q: “Can you deploy in our VPC?”
A: “Yes—Private deployment supports customer-managed networking. The exact topology depends on your environment, but the goal is keeping traffic within your boundary while retaining the same API and operational tooling.”

Q: “Can you run air-gapped / on-prem?”
A: “There’s an on-prem package option for regulated or air-gapped environments, subject to qualification. We’ll evaluate operational requirements (updates, keys, audit exports) with your team.”
Escalate: Simran Kaur (enterprise demo architect) + Naomi Feldman.

Q: “How do upgrades work in Private?”
A: “Controlled releases with pinned versions; you choose when to update. We provide guidance and support plans depending on tier.”


SECTION I — Competitive objections (safe framing)

Q: “Competitor X says they’re faster.”
A: “We’re happy to benchmark, but speed depends on the workload. Our differentiator is making performance predictable in production: consistent tail latency under concurrency, cost controls, and fallbacks. Let’s run a quick eval on your prompts and concurrency profile.”

Q: “Why shouldn’t we self-host?”
A: “You can, but the hidden cost is operational: kernel/runtime tuning, batching, caching, routing, rollouts, observability, and incident response. Redwood packages those into a platform so your team stays focused on product. If you have strict constraints, we can also meet you with Private deployments.”

Q: “Are you just wrapping open-source runtimes?”
A: “We integrate with the ecosystem, but the value is the production platform: orchestration, routing/fallback, pinned rollouts, cost/latency analytics, and deployment consistency across hosted/dedicated/private.”


SECTION J — Live demo troubleshooting (quick scripts)

If the demo tenant is returning 429s / throttling
- Say: “We’re hitting a protective rate limit. Let’s switch to the scripted workload with a lower concurrency and I’ll show how rate limiting behaves and how Dedicated avoids noisy-neighbor constraints.”
- SE action: check quota settings + healthcheck; if needed, swap to backup project namespace.
- Escalate: Markus Klein. Reference: SUP-4127.

If streaming disconnects
- Say: “Streaming is supported; here’s the fallback: we can rerun the request non-streaming to continue the demo and we’ll follow up with client settings and region status.”
- SE action: switch region, reduce concurrency, use the backup script output if necessary.
- Escalate: Sean Gallagher.

If Console dashboards are empty
- Say: “This tenant uses synthetic events to populate dashboards; we’ll trigger the generator so you see realistic distributions.”
- SE action: run traffic generator + refresh time range/project selector.
- Escalate: Markus Klein. Reference: SUP-4189.

If auth/RBAC blocks access
- Say: “Looks like a role mapping issue. We can proceed with the live API portion while we fix Console access, and I’ll send screenshots of the Console views after.”
- Escalate: Ethan Park + Markus Klein. Reference: INT-993.


SECTION K — Follow-up templates (paste-ready)

Template: Security follow-up
“Thanks again. Per your questions: we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, encryption in transit/at rest, audit logs, and configurable retention controls. Here’s our demo security FAQ (internal link for now; we can provide the customer-safe packet on request). Happy to schedule a security review with our security lead.”

Template: Pricing follow-up
“Pricing depends on model + volume + latency targets. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity for predictable throughput/isolation; Private is a platform fee + support tier. If you share your expected QPS, context/output lengths, and preferred regions, we’ll propose a package and can run a quick benchmark on your prompts.”

Template: POC next steps
“To make a POC successful, we typically align on: (1) prompt set + eval criteria, (2) target latency/throughput under concurrency, (3) rollout/fallback policy, (4) observability needs, and (5) security requirements (SSO, audit export, residency). If you’re aligned, we can provision a POC tenant and get started this week.”
